question: Can I take my whole program online from outside Canada and still be eligible for a PGWP?
answer: Yes, you can take your whole program online from outside Canada and still be eligible for a PGWP, but only if you meet the criteria for the temporary COVID-19 policy. According to the sources, you must have been enrolled in a PGWP-eligible program, outside Canada, and not have traveled to Canada because of the COVID-19 pandemic, but still able to take online courses. (Source: [2] Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

question: I studied 4 months at a school that isn't a DLI and then 6 months at a DLI. Can I get a PGWP?
answer:
According to the sources, since you transferred from a non-DLI to a DLI, only the time you spent studying at the DLI will be counted. You must spend at least 8 months at the DLI to be eligible for a PGWP. (Source: [1] Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

Since you only spent 6 months at the DLI, you do not meet the eligibility requirement.

question: My study permit had already expired when I applied for my PGWP. Can I work while I wait for the decision?
answer:
According to the sources, if your study permit had already expired when you applied for your PGWP, you may still be eligible to work while waiting for the decision. 

(Source: [2] Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

You can either apply for a visitor record to stay in Canada longer or leave Canada and apply for your PGWP. If you stay in Canada and let your permit expire, you must apply to restore your status as a student to apply for your PGWP. To restore your status, you must pay additional fees.

question: My program is 3 years long. Do I only need to show money for the first year of my studies?
answer:
You must show you have enough financial resources for the first year of your studies, and for programs more than a year long, you must also tell us how you plan to pay for the full duration of your studies. (Source: [1] Study permit: Get the right documents - Proof of financial support, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html)

You must provide us with documents that prove you have the required funds available for all the costs listed above, including the full duration of your studies. (Source: [2] Study permit: Get the right documents - Proof of financial support, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html)

For programs more than a year long, you must also tell us how you plan to pay for the full duration of your studies. (Source: [3] Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot : Get the right documents, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/fmc-student-pilot/get-documents.html)

You must give enough proof to show that you meet all the financial capacity requirements, including the full duration of your studies. (Source: [4] Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot : Get the right documents, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/fmc-student-pilot/get-documents.html)

Therefore, no, you do not only need to show money for the first year of your studies.

question: Can I get a Canadian visitor visa when I land at the airport in Canada?
answer:
You can apply for a new visitor visa from within Canada if you meet all the conditions below:
- You’re already in Canada.
- You already hold a valid study or work permit.
- You want to leave and return to Canada .
- Your existing visitor visa is expired or was valid for only one entry.

(Source: [1] Visitor record: Travelling outside Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay/return.html)

However, a valid Temporary Resident Visa is not a guarantee of entry into Canada. An officer at the port of entry will decide if you still meet the requirements for admission when you arrive.

(Source: [3] Guide 5256 - Applying for a visitor visa (temporary resident visa) - paper application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5256-applying-visitor-visa-temporary-resident-visa.html)

question: I got a new passport. Is the eTA linked to my old passport still valid for my next flight?
answer:
According to source [4]: Electronic travel authorization (eTA): Citizens from some visa-required countries, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta/eligibility/eta-x.html

When you fly to Canada, you must travel with the same passport you used to apply for an eTA. If you get a new passport after applying for an eTA, you must apply for a new eTA with your new passport.

So, the eTA linked to your old passport is not valid for your next flight.
